question.text: Partly paid-up units in an AIF represent:

answer.text: The portion of committed capital that has been invested (drawn down) by the investor in the AIF
Units held only by the sponsor

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (p.43) states that partly paid-up units represent the portion of committed capital that has been invested by the investor in the AIF or scheme. That "invested capital" is the amount drawn down by the manager from the investor's overall commitment through drawdown notices/capital calls (pp.50-51). The Trap: Partly paid-up units are not valueless, free distribution units, or units restricted to the sponsor — they simply reflect the share of the investor's commitment that has actually been called and paid in. Note: Source references: NISM Series XIX-A workbook p.43 (partly paid-up units = portion of committed capital invested) and pp.50-51 (drawdown mechanics; investors need cash resources available during the agreed drawdown period).
